correctness.rationale: The positive-ray normal form and its t<0 cyclic relabeling cover every strictly convex six-vertex polygon with opposite sides parallel. Direct symbolic shoelace gives A(P)=ab+ac+bc+bt-t²/2, independently checked with a computer algebra identity, and difference-body edge sums yield A(P-P)=4A(P)+t². The Wigner midpoint triangle has oriented area -t²/8. The published containment LP yields s=(U+2)/(U+1) for t>0 with U=x+y+z>0. For fixed U, exact pairwise-product maximization xy+xz+yz≤U²/3 with equality x=y=z and strict infimum zero proves both sharp conditional interval boundaries, all realizations and exact half-variance stability. The independent hull and caustic script passed 964 exact rational polygons including negative t, without treating finite tests as a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The main theorem conditions two affine area invariants on the exact Minkowski asymmetry s of genuine six-sided CPPOSes. The 2026 Giblin–Janeczko–Zwierzyński paper uses difference-body area to bound reflection energy, but not its fixed-s profile. The 2026 Konicer et al. paper derives Wigner and symmetral area identity plus global 1/4 bound, without conditional optimization in s. The published exact hexagonal Minkowski-asymmetry formula is cited as a prior input, not a new contribution. Published Wigner area records for 8,10,12 equiangular constant-width polygons are not implications of a six-sided profile indexed by s. The 2013 original CPPOS geometry, classical Rogers–Shephard global inequality, and operator characterization do not establish this conditional spectrum. Searches identified no exact equivalence, while historical priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: A broader historical source outside current search indices might contain the conditional six-sided profile or a stronger implication.

value.rationale: The question couples two canonical affine invariants on the natural full six-sided CPPOS class and answers a motivated conditional geometric extremal problem, sharpening the classical unconditional Rogers–Shephard and Wigner-caustic bounds for each exact asymmetry. It supplies a complete interval, an interior symmetry-rigid extremizer, a degenerate upper mechanism, and a globally exact quadratic variance identity. The lower and upper departures from central symmetry have differing second/first-order behavior. This is a structural classification beyond numerical sampling or a routine restatement of the earlier asymmetry formula.
